name: Vlog timestamps
sound: Pump It, The Black Eyed Peas
what: A quick run of clips from a day or a job, each labelled with a time or a step (the setting, the fuel, the tools), joined by swipe transitions with no voiceover.
origin: An older track picked up by small businesses and runners from Sept 2026. Later listed the format on 23 Oct 2026 and Buffer on 3 Nov 2026. Original creator not found.
usage: 692K Instagram reels on the audio (5 Nov 2026), up from 682K on Postdom (2 Nov); top reel on the audio page 295K views
brand_use: A day in the life of the business: open up, coffee, tools, first customer, finished job. Suits salons, cafes, trades and studios, and any team with a behind-the-scenes story.
risk: Major-label track, so it may be restricted on business accounts. Check in-app or run the same format on a cleared sound.

examples.note: top reel on the audio page, runner labelling coffee, shoes and fuel (@edmond.running, 22 Oct 2026)
behind the scenes of a designer, labelled 'The Architect' (@laledesign.me, 15 Oct 2026)

notes: Count is lifetime for a long-standing song, so many of the 692K reels will not be this format. Later describes timestamps, Buffer describes labels; the cover frames I saw show labels and no timestamps, and I could only view covers. No big posts: mainly a small-business format. Instagram shows only 12 reels logged out, so 'top' means top of those. Business-account access could not be checked logged out. Plays are the view counts on Instagram's audio page grid (5 Nov 2026); likes and the song on each reel come from its embed page, which also reports a lower video_view_count (about half), so plays depend on which Instagram figure you read.

name: Small text zoom
sound: DROP IT LIKE ITS HOT x STAYIN ALIVE (ALTÉGO MIX), altego_music (original audio)
what: A tiny line of text sits in the scene, then the camera zooms in until it fills the frame: 'You're doing amazing sweetie', 'You're a good mama'. Usually an encouraging message aimed at one type of person.
origin: Mash-up uploaded by altego_music; the biggest reels are from 7 to 9 Oct 2026, on parenting accounts. Later listed it on 30 Oct 2026 and Buffer on 3 Nov 2026. Original reel not found.
usage: 570K Instagram reels on the audio (5 Nov 2026); top reel 8.2M views, 534.6K likes
brand_use: Pick one audience and say something kind or cheeky to them: 'You're nearly at payday', 'Your dog thinks you're great'. Later also suggests it for hinting at an announcement. Cheap to make and built to be sent to a friend.
risk: Tagged original audio, but it is a mash-up of two commercial songs, so don't assume it is cleared. Sincere messages from a brand can feel forced, so keep it light.

examples.note: top reel on the audio page, 'You're doing amazing sweetie' (@mrsemilynicholas, 9 Oct 2026)
'You're a cool Dad', the example Buffer uses (@dontdillydally_, 16 Oct 2026)

notes: Status is a judgement: there is no earlier dated count to measure growth, the biggest reels are about four weeks old, and the round-ups only listed it from 30 Oct. No brand example among the 12 reels Instagram shows logged out; Kerry Washington used it for a voting message (602K views, 49,266 likes), left out as political. No TikTok version checked. Plays are the view counts on Instagram's audio page grid (5 Nov 2026); likes and the song on each reel come from its embed page, which also reports a lower video_view_count (about half), so plays depend on which Instagram figure you read.

name: Not every angel walks the runway
what: On-screen text says not every angel gets the Victoria's Secret runway, over a clip of you at your desk or on your commute, walking like one anyway. A dreamier version sets the song over a too-pretty view or a glam look.
origin: JADE's 2024 single came back after Kylie Jenner's Victoria's Secret show walk (18 Oct 2026, InMusicBlog). JADE's own TikTok about it (20 Oct) is the most-played post checked on the sound.
usage: 263K Instagram reels on the audio and 128.6K TikTok videos on the sound (5 Nov 2026); Instagram was 241K on Postdom (2 Nov) and 211K on SocialPilot; top post 23.7M plays
brand_use: The workplace joke suits any team: 'not every angel walks the runway, some of us do the BAS'. Tourism and hospitality can use the dreamy version, as @australia did for Melbourne: a hotel's best view, a ring box opening, a finished nail set.
risk: Major-label track, so it may be restricted on business accounts. The joke leans on one celebrity moment, so it will date quicker than the dreamy version.

examples.note: most-played TikTok checked on the sound, JADE on Kylie Jenner (20 Oct 2026)
joint top reel on the Instagram audio page, 'not all angels can be in the VSFS, I'm in Excel' (@kelsey_paul, 20 Oct 2026)
brand use, Melbourne reel from @australia (27 Oct 2026); plays from Postdom, 2 Nov

notes: usage_n adds the Instagram and TikTok page counts, as the Money can't buy happiness entry does. TikTok counts disagree: the sound page showed 128.6K videos, Tokchart about 83.6K in late Oct, and InMusicBlog over 270,000 creations on 23 Oct. I used the sound page. Rising on Instagram's own counts: 241K to 263K in three days. The count covers all uses of the song, not just the angel joke. The name is mine, not an established trend name. @australia's embed page shows 83,792 views against Postdom's 383,048, and 23,212 likes against Postdom's 23,784; likes here are the embed figure. Business-account access could not be checked logged out. Plays are the view counts on Instagram's audio page grid (5 Nov 2026); likes and the song on each reel come from its embed page, which also reports a lower video_view_count (about half), so plays depend on which Instagram figure you read.

name: Upside Down hand transition
what: Mouth the lyric, hit the hand gesture and cut to the reveal: new hair, a day-to-night outfit or a big travel view.
origin: Later listed it on 2 Oct 2026; the biggest reels are from 4 to 7 Oct 2026. Buffer still had it on 3 Nov and CreatorDB on 4 Nov. Original creator not found.
usage: 352K Instagram reels on the audio (5 Nov 2026); top reel 3.9M views, 272.8K likes
brand_use: A before-and-after with one hand gesture: the tired room to the styled room, day look to night look, raw ingredient to finished plate. Fashion, beauty, homewares and tourism fit best.
risk: Major-label track, so it may be restricted on business accounts. The transition works on a cleared sound.

examples.note: top reel on the audio page, Victoria Falls travel reel (@abeunseen, 4 Oct 2026)
day-to-night outfit reveal tagging Cult Gaia and Alexander Wang (@valslooks, 17 Oct 2026)

notes: CreatorDB lists 127K reels and calls it Rising, but Instagram's page shows 352K, so its figure is out of date. I saw cover frames only, so the transition itself rests on Later and Buffer; the two biggest reels are travel clips and I could not confirm they show it. @valslooks' caption says 'day and night'. Business-account access could not be checked logged out. Plays are the view counts on Instagram's audio page grid (5 Nov 2026); likes and the song on each reel come from its embed page, which also reports a lower video_view_count (about half), so plays depend on which Instagram figure you read.

name: Toggle on
sound: Original audio, sviola_handmade (Mix: Kanye West, Touch The Sky, plus Instagram click sounds)
what: An iPhone-style ON/OFF switch sits above a poster or photo. A finger flips it on and the news appears: a launch, an event, a new series.
origin: Italian knitwear maker @sviola_handmade posted the audio with a pattern launch on 7 Oct 2026, which is also the top reel on it. Later listed it on 30 Oct 2026 and Buffer on 3 Nov 2026.
usage: 27K Instagram reels on the audio (5 Nov 2026); top reel 4.8M views
brand_use: Made for announcements: flip the switch to reveal a sale date, a new store, a menu or a booking window. Small brands are already doing this, and it needs only a static poster and a finger.
risk: The audio's own title credits a Kanye West song, so check the client is comfortable, and don't assume it is cleared because it's tagged original audio. The switch works with a click sound alone.

examples.note: origin of the audio and top reel on it, knitting pattern launch (@sviola_handmade, 7 Oct 2026)
brand use, shoe shop trunk show announcement (@chattanoogashoe, 12 Oct 2026)
brand use, skincare event announcement (@infyve.beauty, 12 Oct 2026)

notes: Smallest count here but the most brand-ready format: the reels I checked on the audio are businesses announcing something. Status rests on round-ups adding it from 30 Oct; there is no earlier dated count. Views are high against likes on the brand posts, and I can't say why. @sviola_handmade is the earliest of the 12 reels shown logged out and the audio is theirs, but I can't rule out an earlier one. No TikTok version checked. Plays are the view counts on Instagram's audio page grid (5 Nov 2026); likes and the song on each reel come from its embed page, which also reports a lower video_view_count (about half), so plays depend on which Instagram figure you read.
